# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 84 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 49 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_084_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 84

**1** Jesus said: "When you see your likeness, you rejoice.

**2** But when you see your images that came into existence before you — which neither die nor become manifest — how much will you be able to bear?"

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Your likeness"** — *eine*: the mirror-image, the earthly reflection of the self — seeing it produces joy.

**"Your images that came into existence before you"** — the pre-existent archetypes or heavenly doubles — these neither die nor manifest in the ordinary world.

**"How much will you be able to bear?"** — a challenge: can the earthly self endure confrontation with its pre-existent, deathless archetype? This connects to Platonic-Gnostic concepts of the soul's heavenly image predating its earthly incarnation.

**Theological Note:** EMET preserves "likeness" and "images" as distinct terms; LOGOS and PNEUMA both agree on the core structure. The saying moves from everyday self-recognition (the mirror) to the overwhelming encounter with one's eternal form.
